note: Session-only finding from live value scanning + user's manual Cheat Engine address list, cross-referenced with camera-rotation-invariance and jump-height discriminators. This is a raw process address, NOT yet a stable module-base+offset or AOB signature — it WILL change on game restart. Needs a pointer-scan pass to become restart-stable before shipping.

history.wrongAddress_cameraPosition: 0x3b8c4c60 (struct base) - confirmed to track camera, not player, via camera-rotation test. Superseded.
history.correctAddress_playerPosition: 0x47a55e10 (struct base) - validated: (1) unchanged during camera-only rotation, (2) increases/decreases correctly with jump/landing on the height field, (3) both horizontal fields show large smooth movement-correlated changes while height stays flat during flat-ground walking.

sessionOnlyAddress.note: Confirmed via CE 'find what writes': the writing code addresses this struct as [base + 0x40]. Base held in RBX/RCX. Position floats are at base+0x40/0x44/0x48. This base reallocates — needs a static pointer path (pointer scan targeting 0x47a55dd0).

writingInstruction: near DD2.exe+0x54BB683 (RIP at post-write addss xmm3,xmm4; actual movss [rbx+40] just before)
persistentAnchor: RSI = 0x1D4B83500 stayed byte-identical across the original capture, a save-reload, AND a full DD2 restart — a deterministic singleton (player manager?). Fallback anchor if the pointer chain ever breaks.

stablePointerChain.note: Found via CE pointer scan, narrowed through a full DD2 restart + 2 reloads (18 survivors), all validated live by testChains.js. Resolves to the struct base; position at base+0x40/0x44/0x48. CE offset order: deref [moduleBase+staticOffset], then apply offsets[0..n-1] each with a deref, add offsets[n] last without deref.

staticLocalPosition.note: MODULE-STATIC copies of the player's LOCAL (cell-relative) position — no pointer chain needed. Layout is a Vec3: x@+0, h@+4, y@+8. These re-center to 0 (unlike the pointer-chain struct at +0x40, which carries a constant -8/-8 offset on x/y and -6.7 on h: static = chain + 8). Two verified mirrors, values identical.
staticLocalPosition.notAMirror: 0x0F8FD268 — layout is [h, -x, y] (x is SIGN-FLIPPED). Different struct; do not read x from it.

globalPosition.note: SOLVED 2026-07-11. The ABSOLUTE world position lives in memory as a Vec3 (X @ +0, Y @ +8; the +4 field is NOT on the 128-grid, ignore it). global = local + k*128. Reading it directly fully solves floating origin: no dead reckoning, zero drift, teleport-proof. WIRED INTO THE APP (src/main/index.js).
globalPosition.foundVia: src/main/globalHunt.js identified the live global (lockstep filter d(global)==d(local) between crossings, then a boundary crossing separates global from local). Then a CE + Node pointer scan against a stable heap copy, narrowed across 3 reloads, validated by src/main/pointerScan.js.

stableChain.note: PRIMARY (wired). Validated across TELEPORT + reload + full game restart (ASLR). Reaches the gameplay-live global copy. Offset order = CE display order = resolvePointerChain order.

fallbackChain.note: On a DIFFERENT static base/structure; also teleport+restart stable. Used if primary fails/inconsistent on a tick.

globalPosition.teleportLesson: An earlier chain (0BB0E1D0 -> [0x40,0x20,0x190,0x3F8,0x88,0x3E0]) survived reload/restart but read GARBAGE after a teleport until the in-game map was opened — it threaded a MAP-OWNED copy only refreshed when the map is up. Always test chains with a teleport WITHOUT opening the map; keep only ones that stay consistent (reach the gameplay-live copy).
globalPosition.candidateFiles: global.chains2.json (teleport-robust set, wired), global.chains.json (earlier map-owned set)
globalPosition.notInPlayerStruct: Separate allocation ~100MB from the local player struct; the global lives in its own object reached by the chain above.

backupCandidate.note: Also validated (camera-rotation-invariant, real X/Z movement tracking, height stays flat on flat ground) — likely another duplicate copy of the same player position. Not currently used; kept as a fallback if 0x47a55e10 stops resolving.

cameraPosition.note: SOLVED 2026-07-13. The camera's position, as a Vec3 laid out like the player's (x @+0, height @+4, y @+8). The camera LOOKS AT the player, so the horizontal vector camera->player IS the view direction: heading = atan2(player.x - cam.x, player.y - cam.y). That is a real FACING angle, available while standing still — unlike the movement-derived heading, which has nothing to report when you stop. WIRED INTO THE APP (src/main/index.js ships `facing` on the position feed; it drives the marker arrow and the overlay's heading-up rotation). Facing crosses into map space as a look-ahead POINT, never as an angle — see FINDINGS.md.
cameraPosition.foundVia: tools/cameraHunt.js. Not a value scan — there is no value to scan for. The camera is the one thing in memory ON A LEASH: it stays a few units from the player through walking, sprinting, teleports and cell-boundary snaps, so the search key is a RELATION (a Vec3 that never leaves the leash), and float soup walks off it within a few metres. Then rotation separates it from everything else that follows the player: stand still, swing the mouse, and the camera is what MOVES WHILE THE PLAYER FLOATS ARE FROZEN.

existsInBothFrames.note: Like the player, the camera is stored in BOTH the cell-local frame and the absolute one. Verified, exactly: camGlobal - camLocal = (640.00, -1024.00) = (5, -8) cells = precisely the player's own cell offset, and the camera's offset from the player was identical in both frames to 3 decimals. Same camera, two coordinate systems. USE THE GLOBAL ONE — it sidesteps the floating origin, and it is what the app already reads for the player.

stableChain.note: GLOBAL-frame camera. Narrowed 8148 -> 7529 (teleport) -> 5595 (save reload) -> 285 (FULL GAME RESTART), then live-verified: resolves through the restart, holds a constant 5.4u radius while the heading sweeps a full circle. The shortest surviving chain of the 285; the 6-hop ones nearly all share its tail [.., 0x18, 0x18, 0x5f8, 0x800], which is the camera object's real structure reached from many entry points.

cameraPosition.candidateFiles: tools/camera.global.chains.json (285 restart-survivors, the wired one is in here), tools/camera.local.chains.json (the local-frame scan — kept only as a record; prefer global)
cameraPosition.notAStatic: The camera is NOT in module-static memory. All 92MB of DD2.exe's writable .data was swept and every leashed Vec3 there was walked off the leash within a few metres. Don't look for a static mirror the way staticLocalPosition has one — it isn't there.
cameraPosition.notTheBones: A first pass ranked candidates by TIGHTEST leash and returned 548 hits sitting 0.3-0.7u from the player, all of them 'moving while you stood still'. Those are SKELETON BONES: the idle animation sways them while the root position is frozen, so they pass the rotation test exactly like a camera does. What separates them is how far they ROAM while you stand still — swing the mouse and the camera sweeps metres of arc at constant radius, while a bone jiggles centimetres. Rank by roam, not by proximity.

dungeonZoneIndex.note: Found via CE value-scanning (2026-07-13). insideFlag is WIRED INTO THE APP (src/main/index.js, src/main/areaTracker.js) and replaced the doorway-proximity guess for the in/out decision. zoneIndex is NOT yet usable — see its note. Module-static, no pointer chain (same category of read as staticLocalPosition), so expected restart-stable by construction; the user observed both values unchanged across a full game restart. Not yet tested across a DD2 game-version update.

values.0: overworld — CONFIRMED live 2026-07-13 (was only presumed before)
values.2: ALSO inside (user-observed) — some second kind of interior; what distinguishes it from 1 is not yet known. Both non-zero values are treated as 'inside'; tools/zoneLog.js is collecting the data to find out what 2 actually is.

insideFlag.note: Does not change between dungeon floors. Persists across full game restart. This is what the app keys 'am I inside' on. LAGS THE MAP: it does not flip the instant the in-game map changes — a walk out of a cave showed the map already switched while the flag still read 1. It settles once you are properly out. Don't conclude from one sample that it's stale (we did, briefly, and were wrong).

zoneIndex.note: The GAME's own dungeon id. NOT mapgenie's numbering — mapgenie's subregion ids run 2441-2514, while observed game ids are 18, 69, 2010. The two do not coincide and a mapping table has to be BUILT. Until one exists, zoneIndex cannot name a dungeon and the app instead picks the NEAREST KNOWN ENTRANCE from mapgenie's portal graph. Run tools/zoneLog.js while playing: it pairs (insideFlag, zoneIndex) with the nearest entrance's name on every transition, which is exactly the table needed. Once complete, 'which dungeon' becomes a lookup, stops depending on the world affine, and reaches the two dungeons mapgenie has no entrance for.
zoneIndex.keyOn: the PAIR (insideFlag, zoneIndex) — the flag selects an id namespace: flag-1 ids are small (18, 69), flag-2 ids are four-digit and sequential (2010, 2011).
zoneIndex.status: COLLECTING — 4 of ~74. See tools/zoneLog.js and zone_log.txt (gitignored).

roomHash.note: NOT USABLE FOR FLOORS — dead end, recorded so it is not retried. It is an id for a streaming CELL, not a room and not a floor: the same hash (1bc90b46, ae32b49d) appears at h=-13.7 AND h=-5.2 in The Gracious Hand's Vaults, and two of them flicker back and forth three times a second while you stand still on a boundary. It IS deterministic across sessions (walking a cave one way and back gives the identical hashes in reverse), which is what made it look usable — it was tried as a learned roomHash->floor key and it fought the player, flipping the floor in stairwells until every room was marked ambiguous. Floors come from the LocalArea pointer instead (src/main/localAreaReader.js), whose id is unique per (area, floor); the older HEIGHT-learning path was also retired. See FINDINGS. Still read and logged by tools/zoneLog.js.

unknownFloat12.note: 0.0 in the overworld; inside a dungeon it wanders (0.46-0.75 observed) rather than stepping. Not an index. Logged by zoneLog.js in case it turns out to mean something; a blend/fog/darkness factor is the obvious guess.

pointerChainCandidates.note: Cheat Engine pointer scan surfaced multiple heap chains all resolving to 14FA62CB0 — redundant now that the target is known to be a plain module-static address (moduleBase + 0xFA62CB0 = 0x14FA62CB0 for a typical 0x140000000 load base), so none of these are needed or were validated. Kept only as a record of what CE found.

floorHeights.note: RETIRED. Floors were once told apart by HEIGHT, learned per dungeon and stored in config/areas.json under floorHeights — but the height fed to it was LOCAL (rebased per streaming cell), so a floor could read '100u off itself' across a cell boundary. Replaced by the LocalArea pointer (src/main/localAreaReader.js): its id is unique per (area, floor) and immune to falls/lifts/teleports, so nothing height-based is needed. Neither `floorHeights` nor its PageUp/PageDown teach-keys exist in the code any more. Kept as a record of why the height path was a dead end. Measured floor gaps at the time: 5.8u (The Gracious Hand's Vaults) to 16.6u (Forgotten Tunnel), with up to 4u of wander within one floor.
